title: ‘Why not declare Mt Everest a protest site?’: CJP leaders say whole country will become Jantar Mantar - Moneycontrol.com
full_text:
Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest venue in the national capital, with Delhi Police removing it from the list and drawing criticism from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Abhijeet Dipke.
Questioning the decision in a post on X, Ranka asked, “Why not declare Mt Everest as the designated protest site?”
Dipke also criticised the move. He alleged that Jantar Mantar had been turned into a “war zone” and described the decision as an attempt to restrict protests.
Dipke posted: “They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it’s no longer a protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone ... Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!”
On Monday, Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a venue for protests and demonstrations. Three locations will replace it: Ramlila Ground in central Delhi, Burari Ground in north Delhi and CBD Ground in east Delhi, the police order stated.
The decision was announced under Standing Order No. L&O/48/2026, issued on October 11 by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar. According to the order, it follows recommendations by a committee constituted by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to examine alternative venues where citizens can exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.
The order partially modifies Standing Order No. 48/2022, which was issued on April 28, 2022. Delhi Police said detailed and revised standard operating procedures (SOPs) for demonstrations at the three new locations would be issued separately.

The change marks a shift in the capital’s protest geography, as Jantar Mantar has long been one of Delhi’s best-known sites for demonstrations. The decision comes amid heightened security around central Delhi, following recent protests over alleged electoral roll irregularities and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
